grounding.states: Well made and third-party tested, with solid quality control
grounding.from: Quality control looks solid. Both formulas are third-party tested and NSF Certified for Sport
Sources agree it is well made, tested and tastes decent for most people.
It also flagged key ingredient amounts hidden in proprietary blends and several underdosed ingredients.

grounding.states: No independent clinical evidence for its benefit claims
grounding.from: I found no independent clinical evidence for its benefit claims.

grounding.states: One of the most expensive all-in-one supplements on the market
grounding.from: Live it Up's dietitian (a competing brand, about 57 days old) called it one of the most expensive all-in-one supplements on the market

value.answer: Mostly overrated, I'd say. It's well made, third-party tested, and most people find it tastes decent. But several blends are underdosed, some key amounts are hidden in proprietary blends, and I couldn't find any independent clinical evidence for its benefit claims. A dietitian at a competing brand called it one of the most expensive all-in-one supplements out there. If you like the convenience and can afford it, fine, but it doesn't deliver enough to justify the price.
